title: A Theoretical Study of (Hyper) Self-Attention through the Lens of Interactions: Representation, Training, Generalization
reviewed_version: publisher proceedings version at retrieval; immutable local SHA-256
inspection_outcome: Three Major and one Minor demonstrated findings; conditional central results supported
summary: Shared-embedding approximation counterexample, impossible covariance justification, and incorrect HyperAttention summation domain; localized summed invariant error. Conditional convergence and coefficient identification independently supported.
limitations: No training, dataset/weight download, or benchmark reproduction.
Not exhaustive over every application, nonlinear approximation, and lower-bound claim in 54 pages.
No separate visible UI model label or conversation URL exposed.

problems.title: False shared-embedding approximation bound
problems.claim: Uniform error bounded by zeta1 L sigma_(d+1)(F).
problems.assumptions: S={a,b}; d=d2=1; L=2; F=[[0,1],[0,0]]; w=(1,1); arbitrary real shared embedding.
problems.check: aa requires t*u=0; ab then cannot output target one despite zero singular tail.
problems.result: No embedding and parameters satisfy the stated bound.
problems.impact: Invalidates low-dimensional extension used to justify central representation theory.
problems.correction: Proved common-subspace bound (1); does not recover original singular-tail guarantee.

problems.title: Impossible covariance assumption and invalid centering argument
problems.location: Assumption E.1/Theorem E.2/Remark E.3 pp.35-37; main pp.5-6
problems.claim: Positive-definite count covariance justifies data versatility under natural fixed-length sampling.
problems.assumptions: All actual count vectors have fixed coordinate sum L*, including conditional rows.
problems.check: Cov(s)*1=0 identically; uniform two-token example has eigenvalues 0,4/9. Centering rank counterexample uses scalar equiprobable 0,2.
problems.result: E.1 is impossible for the model; rank preservation used in E.2 proof is false.
problems.counterevidence: Uncentered count matrices can have full rank; abstract E.2 high-probability conclusion is not disproved; conditional main theorems survive.
problems.impact: Removes stated probabilistic justification of central full-rank condition.
problems.correction: Finite-support span assumption and union bound (2) independently proved.

problems.title: HyperAttention reordering drops triangular restriction
problems.location: Definition 6.1 p.7; Appendix G.3 Eqs.42-43 p.44; G.5 p.45; main p.8
problems.claim: Equation (43) is efficient exact reordering of defined HyperAttention.
problems.assumptions: d=R=d2=1,L=2,all factors and inputs one; valid symmetric rank-one case.
problems.check: Defined triangular sum is 3; factored Cartesian sum is 4.
problems.counterevidence: Cartesian formula is valid for unrestricted variant; training theorem and existence of efficient correction survive; experimental implementation not available.
problems.impact: Invalid exact derivation directly supports efficient proposed architecture.
problems.correction: Prefix-sum restricted linear identity (3) proved and integer cross-checked.

problems.title: Summed coefficient invariant is not sufficient for equivalence
problems.location: Corollary 4.9 p.6; counterevidence Eq.30 p.33, Cor.D.3 p.35, captions pp.53-54
problems.claim: Equal summed T_mu,k iff functionally equivalent.
problems.check: Both T=(1,1) but aa outputs (2,2) vs (0,0).
problems.result: Summing over key-state loses relevant information.
problems.counterevidence: Appendix and actual figure captions use unsummed coefficients; no demonstrated effect on checked training/generalization theorem or empirical diagnostic.
problems.correction: Retain A_mu,nu,k; sufficient and identifiable under count rank/all-sequence probes.

repair_verification: Analytic proofs of common-subspace error bound, finite-support full-rank union bound, prefix-sum triangular contraction, and unsummed invariant; numeric/exact arithmetic cross-checks executed.

unresolved_claims.claim: Multi-layer HyperFeatureAttention expressivity assertion in Remark F.6
unresolved_claims.reason: Quantifier analysis not completed; not promoted to Problem.
